rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command follows the command to thank God for His blessings and asks for their continued increase, as in 14:7.
rows.anchor: عطف على تفريع الأمر بالشكر على النعم أمر بطلب استمرار نعم الله تعالى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghbah is seeking the attainment of what one loves; normally the sought person takes a direct object and the desired thing is introduced by fī.
rows.anchor: طلب حصول ما هو محبوب وأصله أن يعدى إلى المطلوب منه بنفسه ويعدى إلى الشيء المطلوب ب

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: In 4:127, raghb in the construction with ʿan means turning desire away; ʿĀʾisha explains the phrase by supplying an omitted ʿan before an.
rows.anchor: وذلك تأويل عائشة أم المؤمنين كما تقدم في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb takes ilā here because it includes the sense of turning toward or approaching, like traveling to someone who has what one needs.
rows.anchor: فلتضمينه معنى الإقبال والتوجه تشبيها بسير السائر إلى من عنده حاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “to your Lord” first restricts desire to God alone; this exclusivity befits the greatest quality of a messenger and rules out desiring another.
rows.anchor: أي إليه لا إلى غيره تكون رغبتك فإن صفة الرسالة أعظم صفات الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “desire” is omitted to encompass everything the Prophet might seek: spiritual perfection, the spread of religion, and victory for Muslims.
rows.anchor: ليعم كل ما يرغبه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهل يرغب النبي إلا في الكمال النفساني وانتشار الدين ونصر المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ links the verbs because fronting their complements implies restriction and thereby a conditional sense; this is common, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: رابطة للفعل لأن تقديم المعمول يتضمن معنى الاشتراط والتقييد فإن تقديم المعمول لما أفاد الاختصاص نشأ منه معنى الاشتراط

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a man asked to go out for jihad, the Prophet asked whether he had parents and told him to strive in their service; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites this as a preposed phrase treated conditionally.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن سأل منه أن يخرج للجهاد

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī, citing al-Sayyid’s A Amālī (Ibn al-Shajarī), calls the combination of fāʾ and wāw here one of the most astonishing expressions because fāʾ has other usual syntactic roles.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن « أمالي السيد » ( يعني ابن الشجري ) أن اجتماع الفاء والواو هنا من أعجب كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the restrictive force of the fronted complement is understood as conditional, there is no reason for al-Ṭībī’s puzzlement about the fāʾ and wāw.
rows.anchor: ولا يبقى تعجب بعد ما قررناه

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī and Muslim report from Anas that the Prophet said God had commanded him to recite the sūrah to Ubayy; Ubayy asked whether he had been named and, told yes, wept. Its opening clause names the whole sūrah.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common title in tafsīr and hadith books is Sūrat Lam yakun, shortened to its first word; it is also the familiar name among Tunisian Qurʾān-school students.
rows.anchor: وسميت هذه السورة في معظم كتب التفسير وكتب السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other recorded titles are al-Qayyima, al-Bayyina, Ahl al-Kitāb in Ubayy’s codex, al-Bariyya, and al-Infikāk, making six names in all.
rows.anchor: وسميت في أكثر المصاحف { سورة القيمة } وكذلك في بعض التفاسير

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the more widely held view is that the sūrah is Meccan, as most commentators say.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : الأشهر أنها مكية وهو قول جمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār are reported to classify the sūrah as Medinan.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار هي مدنية

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reverses the attributions: he assigns the Medinan view to the majority and Ibn ʿAbbās, and the Meccan view to Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.
rows.anchor: وعكس القرطبي فنسب القول بأنها مدنية إلى الجمهور وابن عباس والقول بأنها مكية إلى يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: أبو حبة البدري
rows.claim: Abū Ḥabba al-Badrī reports that when the passage was revealed Gabriel told the Prophet that God commanded him to recite it to Ubayy, supporting a Medinan setting.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن كثير عن أحمد بن حنبل بسنده إلى أبي حبة البدري قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī and Ibn Kathīr firmly call it Medinan; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers this because it often rebukes the People of the Book and because of Abū Ḥabba’s report.
rows.anchor: وجزم البغوي وابن كثير بأنها مدنية

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd includes the sūrah among the Medinan revelations.
rows.anchor: وقد عدها جابر بن زيد في عداد السور المدنية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues for a Medinan setting on the ground that the Prophet only confronted the People of the Book there.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دفع إلى مناقضة أهل الكتاب بالدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It ranks 101st in revelation, after al-Ṭalāq and before al-Ḥashr; since Banū al-Naḍīr was in Rabīʿ I, year four, it was revealed in late year three or early year four.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت المائة وإحدى في ترتيب النزول نزلت بعد سورة الطلاق وقبل سورة الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities count eight verses in the sūrah, while the people of Basra count nine.
rows.anchor: وعدد آياتها ثمان عند الجمهور

words: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah rebukes the polytheists and People of the Book for rejecting the Qurʾān and the Messenger, and exposes the contradiction of awaiting the clear proof and then rejecting it.
rows.anchor: أغراضها توبيخ المشركين وأهل الكتاب على تكذيبهم بالقرآن والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the sūrah’s aims are to refute their claim that God required them to remain with their existing religions, warn them of the afterlife, and mark them as the worst creatures.
rows.anchor: وتكذيبهم في ادعائهم أن الله أوجب عليهم التمسك بالأديان التي هم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah praises believers who do good and promises them everlasting bliss, God’s approval, and whatever will satisfy them.
rows.anchor: والثناء على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also extols the Qurʾān above earlier scripture because it contains what the Messenger brought in previous divine books and adds further merit.
rows.anchor: وتخلل ذلك تنويه بالقرآن وفضله على غيره باشتماله على ما في الكتب الإلهية التي جاء بها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من قبل

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī, quoted by Fakhr al-Dīn from his al-Tafsīr al-Basīṭ, calls this verse among the Qurʾān’s hardest in construction and interpretation, saying even leading scholars were baffled; Fakhr says he did not clarify the problem.
rows.anchor: ذكر الفخر عن الواحدي في « التفسير البسيط » له أنه قال : هذه الآية من أصعب ما في القرآن نظما وتفسيرا

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Fakhr reads the omitted complement of “detached” as their disbelief and “the clear proof” as the Messenger; “until” then implies they leave disbelief at his coming, apparently conflicting with 98:4, where division follows the proof’s arrival.
rows.anchor: وأنا أقول : وجه الإشكال أن تقدير الآية : لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة التي هي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr adds that actual history shows neither group ever left disbelief, while the subjunctive verb after ḥattā signals a future event even though the Messenger had arrived years earlier and both groups persisted.
rows.anchor: وأن نصب المضارع بعد { حتى } ينادي على أنه منصوب ب ( أنْ ) مضمرة بعد { حتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the apparent contradictions, the wording cannot be understood by its surface sense; interpreters either recast the whole statement or figuratively interpret one or more of its terms.
rows.anchor: فوجب صرفه عن ظاهره ، إما بصرف تركيب الخبر عن ظاهر الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr groups the interpretations into five bases: recast the whole sentence; reinterpret munfakkīn; reinterpret its omitted complement; take ḥattā conditionally; or reinterpret rasūl, with some allowing two senses for bayyina. Al-Ālūsī and al-Qurṭubī collect most variants, sometimes without attribution.
rows.anchor: ومراجع تأويل الآية تؤول إلى خمسة : الأول : تأويل الجملة بأسرها

rows.speaker: الفراء ونفطويه والزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, Niftawayh, and al-Zamakhsharī take the whole statement as a rebuke and expression of astonishment.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب الفراء ونفطويه والزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya interprets munfakkīn as being released from God’s forbearance and brought to account.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الخروج عن إمهال الله إياهم ومصيرهم إلى مؤاخذتهم ، وهو لابن عطية

rows.speaker: عبد الجبار
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbār supplies “from disbelief” as the omitted complement of munfakkīn.
rows.anchor: بأنه عن الكفر وهو لعبد الجبار

rows.speaker: الفخر وأبو حيان
rows.claim: Fakhr and Abū Ḥayyān supply “from their agreement in disbelief” as the omitted complement of munfakkīn.
rows.anchor: أو عن الاتفاق على الكفر وهو للفخر وأبي حيان

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان الأصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān known as al-Aṣamm, takes the omitted complement to mean they had not ceased bearing witness to the Messenger’s truth before his mission.
rows.anchor: أو منفكين عن الشهادة للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصدق قبل بعثته وهو لابن كيسان عبد الرحمن الملقب بالأصم

rows.speaker: بعض اللغويين
rows.claim: Some linguists understand munfakkīn as no longer alive, that is, doomed to perish.
rows.anchor: أو منفكين عن الحياة ، أي هالكين ، وعزي إلى بعض اللغويين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ḥattā as the connective conditional particle in, giving the sense “even if the clear proof comes to them.”
rows.anchor: أنها بمعنى ( إنْ ) الاتصالية

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim, as cited by Fakhr, takes rasūl to mean angels sent to read divine scrolls, like the People of the Book’s request in 4:153; this reading makes the statement sarcastic.
rows.anchor: وعزاه الفخر إلى أبي مسلم وهو يقتضي صرف الخبر إلى التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators allow two interpretations of the word bayyina.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم جوز في { البينة } وجهين

words: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book described as disbelievers are those who rejected Muḥammad’s message, as in 59:11.
rows.anchor: أنهم كفروا برسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses argue against unbelieving scripturalists and polytheists who used excuses to persist stubbornly in disbelief; the sentence recounts their claim that they would not leave their religion until the promised sign arrived.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآيات وردت مورد إقامة الحجة على الذين لم يؤمنوا من أهل الكتاب وعلى المشركين بأنهم متنصلون من الحق متعللون للإصرار على الكفر عنادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the report as a compound figurative use of an informative sentence for an utterance act, like using a question for rebuke; al-Taftāzānī says no one has identified its precise figure, while al-Sayyid explains it fully.
rows.anchor: استعمال الخبر في الإنشاء والاستفهام في التوبيخ ونحو ذلك الذي قال فيه التفتزاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A close parallel is 9:64: hypocrites were described as fearing exposure, although their apparent fear was pretense, and then told to mock because God would reveal what they hid.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه قوله تعالى : { يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists excused themselves by saying scripture had been sent only to two earlier communities and that they would have been better guided if they had received one.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book also used the excuse that God had covenanted with them not to believe a messenger until he brought a sacrifice consumed by fire.
rows.anchor: الذين قالوا إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both groups widely used this excuse, the future “until the proof comes” precisely recalls what they said before the Messenger arrived and exposes it as an argument against them.
rows.anchor: وشيوعه عن الفريقين قرينة على أن المراد من سياقه دمغهم بالحجة وبذلك كان التعبير بالمضارع المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parallel is 2:89: the People of the Book had sought victory over the disbelievers before the confirming Book came, but rejected what they recognized when it arrived.
rows.anchor: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended force is: you used to claim you would not abandon your religion until the promised sign came.
rows.anchor: أنكم كنتم تقولون لا نترك ما نحن عليه من الدين حتى تأتينا البينة
